C44999.observed: What was checked: whether the Part number box in the new inline row is the same search-as-you-type catalogue box that the existing add-part screen uses. What happened: typing "OIL" into it brought back a list of 24 matching parts from the catalogue, each card showing the part's description, its part number, how many are in stock and which bin they sit in - exactly the same list, in the same shape, as the one the existing add-part flow shows. Nothing about it behaves differently in the inline row.

C45000.observed: What was checked: what happens to the boxes when you pick a part out of that catalogue list, having first typed a description of your own. What happened: with "MY OWN TYPED TEXT" typed into Description, picking a part from the list replaced it with the catalogue's own description and filled the Part number in as well - so your own wording is deliberately replaced by the official one. The cursor then jumped straight to the Qty box, because the other two boxes were already filled in and quantity is the only thing left to type. The cards in the list also showed each part's stock quantity and its bin.
C45000.not_observed: The bin allocation that selecting a part triggers is covered by the Bin Allocation cases (Story 7) and was not exercised here.

C45004.observed: What was checked: whether a part can be saved with only a description and a quantity, leaving the part number blank. What happened: with a description and a quantity of 2 typed in and the Part number box left completely empty, Save worked - the part was added and the line went from ten parts to eleven. Saving with a description but no quantity was refused with the message "Enter a qty to save this part." So the part number really is optional, and the quantity really is required.

C45005.observed: What was checked: where a newly saved part lands in the list, and whether the user is told the save worked. What happened: after saving, the new part appeared as the first row in that line's parts list, above all the parts that were already there, and a green confirmation reading "Part added" appeared and then disappeared on its own without needing to be dismissed.

C45006.observed: What was checked: whether the technician has to press "Add Part" again for each part, or whether the screen keeps them typing. What happened: the moment the save succeeded a fresh, completely empty row opened on the same work order line, and the cursor was already sitting in its Description box - so a technician adding several parts in a row can keep typing without touching the mouse.

C45015.observed: What was checked: whether the message shown when required boxes are empty names all of them at once, and names only the ones that apply to this view. What happened: pressing Save on a completely empty row gave one single message - "Enter a description and qty to save this part." - naming both missing boxes together, in the order they appear on the row. After the description was filled in, pressing Save again gave "Enter a qty to save this part.", naming only what was still missing. No money or category boxes were ever named, because Tech view does not show them.

C45016.observed: What was checked: whether a quantity of zero, or a negative quantity, is rejected with a message of its own. What happened: with a description filled in and the quantity set to 0, Save was refused and the message "Qty must be greater than 0." appeared. Setting the quantity to -3 gave exactly the same message and the same refusal. In both cases the part was not saved.

C45017.observed: What was checked: whether the user can see which box is at fault and is taken to it. What happened: pressing Save on an empty row turned the Description box red and put the cursor straight into it - the first of the two boxes that failed. After the description was filled in and Save was pressed again, the highlight and the cursor both moved on to the Qty box, which was then the first one still at fault.

C45018.observed: What was checked: whether the warning stays on screen after the user fixes what it complained about. What happened: as soon as a description was typed the description warning and its red highlight went away by themselves, leaving only the outstanding quantity warning; and as soon as a valid quantity was typed that warning cleared too, leaving the row with no warnings at all. Neither time did the user have to press Save again to make the message go away.
